title: Learning bass from a Frank Skinner chart
summary: He taught himself using a chart pasted on his bass, despite his double-jointed fingers.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Yeah. And I value that better than any -- I didn't have too much real music training, teaching, anyway. Because I bought a chart, it was a Frank Skinner book, and in the middle of that book was a chart to paste on a bass fiddle. When I first got that bass fiddle I got that chart and I pasted it on the bass fiddle. And it showed the names of each note, and where your fingers should be, and all. And I'd just go home and practice on that.
But I still couldn't it finger it like they -- because of my fingers being double-jointed, you know. But I
found out where the positions were, and I could get on to it.
